Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
241 of 2023 at Police Station-Bahjoi District-Sambhal under Sections 498A, 302, 323 IPC.
The applicant is in jail since 18.07.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court on 24.05.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Bharat Singh, learned counsel assisted by Ms. Aradhna Pandey, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Shrawan Kumar Dubey, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:

sentences.text: 1.The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated with the police investigations and had joined the trial proceedings.
2. The applicant did not influence the witnesses nor tamper with the evidence.
3. The applicant never adopted any dilatory tactics or impeded the process of the trial.
4. The doctor in his testimony before the trial court has deposed that before recording of dying declaration the deceased was drowsy and confused.
5. The deceased become conscious at intermittent stages.
The deceased was rushed to the hospital by her husband Chandrabhan.
However, the aforesaid witness has not been examined or proposed to be introduced as a prosecution witness.
The investigations were biased.
6. The trial has moved at an inordinately slow pace.
The applicant is not responsible for the delay in the trial.

7. Status report sent by the learned trial court in the bail application filed by co-accused in the same criminal case had disclosed that the prosecution proposes to examine 18 witnesses to bring home the charges.
Eight prosecution witnesses including the informant and the doctor material have already been examined.
There is no possibility of the applicant influencing the witnesses or tampering with the evidence.
8. The trial is not likely to conclude in the near future.
9. Inordinate delay in concluding trial had has led to virtually an indefinite imprisonment of the applicant without there being any credible evidence to implicate him in the offence.
10. The rights of the applicant to speedy trial has been violated.
11. The applicant has to gather various defence evidences to be tendered before the trial court to establish his innocence.

12. Continued incarceration of the applicant will disable him from framing an effective defence strategy, gathering evidence in his support thereof and tendering the same before the learned trial court to absolve himself of the charges.

13. This Court in Prabhat Gangwar v. State of U.P. (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.2586 of 2023) while considering the grant of enlarging an accused on bail for preparing his defence and gathering evidence to tender the same before the learned Harpal Singh vs State Of U.P. on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125779103/
2 trial court for establishing his innocence held:
"Nature and gravity of the offence is certainly liable to be considered by the court while considering grant of bail.

entities.text: Prabhat Gangwar v. State of U.P. (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.2586 of 2023)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Harpal Singh vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court has also to factor the likelihood of whether the accused committed the offence while deciding a bail application.

The court also has to determine in the facts of the case whether the accused needs to be set at liberty to frame his defence and gather evidence to refute the prosecution case and establish his innocence.
The bail court has to examine whether continued incarceration would disable the accused from tendering an effective defence of his case.
This is a demand of processual fairness in criminal jurisprudence.
Setting an accused at liberty at large on this ground cannot be applied mechanically in all cases.
The issue has to be considered in the facts and circumstances of each case while doing so.

All relevant facts including the evidences in the record, the conduct of the accused during the investigation as well as trial have to be adverted to before a decision is made in this regard."
14.
Considering the aforesaid parameters in light of the above facts of this case, I am of the opinion that Prabhat Gangwar (supra) is applicable to the facts of this case.
15. Learned AGA contends that the applicant has a criminal history of some more cases.
Rejoining this issue, learned counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant is a poor person.
He is in jail and does not have an effective pairokar.
Hence, details of the cases could not be obtained and stated in the bail application.

However, relying on the records available with the learned AGA and the instructions received from his client, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant was falsely nominated in the said cases.
The said cases do not depict any criminal trait and have no bearing on the instant bail application.
16. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of her influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Harpal Singh be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
